20fb25d88984110a.description:
MailerLite is one of the fastest-growing email marketing services. We help more than 1 million businesses around the world stay in touch with their customers. Today, we are a team of more than 170 dreamers, adventurers, and world travellers passionate about what we do and believe in. And we are ready for another talented person to join the party.
Email marketing is at the heart of what we do, and our own email marketing should be the best proof of that. We're looking for an experienced Senior Email Marketing Manager to join our SEO & Content Team and push our email marketing to a level that our customers, and the wider email marketing community, look up to. If you live and breathe email marketing, experiment with what makes an email engaging and an email list grow, are plugged into where the industry is heading, and are full of ideas most people haven't tried yet, this is a role built for you. 🚀
Why MailerLite?
Wondering why we think you'll love working at MailerLite? Here are 6 reasons!
• 
You'll own the craft, not just the calendar
Every newsletter, campaign and lead magnet you create is a chance to show what great email marketing actually looks like.
• 
You'll get to explore angles others miss Get room to pursue original takes on email marketing. Create content sharp and unique enough to get noticed, talked about, and cited.

• 
You'll have experts at hand
Whenever you’re stuck, your teammates with a wide range of expertise are ready to help. And they’d love for you to share your knowledge too!

• 
You'll grow, develop and evolve
As part of a team that's always looking for new, innovative ways to offer value for our customers, you'll constantly be experimenting, learning, and trying out new things.

• 
You'll take ownership
We expect you to take full responsibility and ownership of your tasks. Team leads avoid micromanaging and minimize interruptions so you can stay focused on your assignments.

• 
You'll pick where you work, every day
We embrace the remote culture. Every day you get to choose what environment makes you most productive.

What you’ll work with

• 
Manage all email campaigns from creation and writing to launch, measurement and optimization

• 
Build and nurture automations to turn prospects into customers and ensure the existing automations are up to date

• 
Own our lead magnets end to end: come up with new ones, write the copy or brief our writers, and keep existing ones accurate and up to date

• 
Identify opportunities to grow our email list. Build the forms, pop-ups and landing pages that turn visitors into subscribers

• 
Keep our MailerLite accounts organized and up-to-date. Build out segmentation and interest groups, and tailor messaging, tone and cadence to different audience segments and industries

• 
Partner with our writers to brief and produce blog content. Review and level up our existing email-marketing content, and push into more advanced topics

• 
Go after original, underexplored angles on email marketing: the kind of ideas that are novel enough to earn citations from LLMs and attention from search engines

• 
Measure email marketing performance and define KPIs. Analyze campaign performance and suggest and implement improvements. 

• 
Keep our sending practices aligned with deliverability standards and industry best practices

• 
Stay genuinely immersed in the email marketing world (new features, research, trends, community chatter) and turn what you learn into content and strategy

• 
Coordinate with our Email Lifecycle Manager so marketing and product/lifecycle email stay consistent without overlapping: you own list growth, segmentation strategy and campaign/newsletter content, while they own the product-side flows

Requirements

• 
4+ years of hands-on experience in email marketing, ideally in a SaaS company where email was a core growth channel

• 
A strong writing portfolio: you can show newsletters or campaigns you've personally written that performed well

• 
Proven experience growing an email list organically, building segmentation, and creating lead magnets

• 
A sharp editorial eye: you can review other people's content and make it meaningfully better

• 
Genuine, ongoing curiosity about email marketing: you follow the space, test new approaches, and have your own point of view

• 
Comfortable both writing hands-on and briefing others: some execution will be supported by our writer team, but you'll personally cover every newsletter and campaign

• 
Experience with MailerLite or other ESPs

• 
4h overlap with CET time zone

What we offer

• 
Yearly gross salary range: $50,000 - $70,000

• 
Remote-first culture with the team working remotely from all over the world

• 
International health insurance provided with coverage in most countries. Monthly healthcare payout available in select countries where coverage is limited

• 
Company-paid retreats. Once per year we gather for a week in a beautiful location to work, learn and have fun together

• 
31 days of vacation per year. We encourage you to unplug and recharge!

• 
12 paid sick days for your physical and mental well-being, no doctor's note required. Parents can use them to care for their sick children

• 
4 creative days. One paid day off per quarter to do something creative and fun

• 
12 parental days per year. Enjoy one paid day off each month to treasure time with your children

• 
Parental leave.100% paid leave when welcoming a new child through birth (3 months maternity, 1 month paternity) or adoption

• 
Joy Budget. Annual allowance to spend on what brings you joy, starting at $1,000 per year and increasing over time

• 
MacBook and other tools that'll help you do your job efficiently

20f9ee2ccfc7b970.description: ## About SleekSky SleekSky builds and runs software for clients who want to scale their technology without heavy overhead. We work in dedicated teams with a startup-inspired culture and a bias for agility, ownership, and continuous improvement. We combine professional depth with real room to learn, decide, and build things that last. ## The role Most product roles at three to five years hand you a backlog to groom and a roadmap someone else set. This one hands you part of a live product and asks you to work out what should happen to it. You'll own areas of a healthcare platform we build and run for a US client, with real organisations using it all day and real patients on the other end. A problem might arrive as a complaint, a number that moved for no obvious reason, or an operations team doing something by hand forty times a day. You take it all the way: - Work out what's actually happening - Decide whether it needs an answer, a fix, or a change worth making - Write the requirement engineering builds from - Stay with it while it's built - Go back and check it did what you said it would It's part product management, part customer engineering, and part sitting with data until it tells you something. It's wide on purpose. ## What you'll own - **Areas of the product, end to end.** You decide what happens next in a part of a live platform, and you're answerable for whether it was worth doing. - **The customer's problem, from complaint to diagnosis.** Our customers are large US healthcare organisations, and their problems arrive as complaints, not specifications. Working out what's actually wrong is yours before anything else happens. - **The requirement engineering builds from.** Written down, with product decisions made and engineering decisions deliberately left open, so engineers can start without you in the room and know which questions are still yours. - **The numbers, watched rather than reported.** Nobody sends you a dashboard each morning. Knowing what normal looks like, noticing when it stops, and finding out why before a customer tells you is part of every day. - **The decision about what not to build.** More requests arrive than can be built. Deciding which ones don't get built, telling the person who asked, and defending the ranking is the hardest part of the job and the one that matters most. ## What you'll bring - **3–5 years in product management**, or an adjacent role where decisions were genuinely yours: business analysis, solution engineering, customer success with real product influence, or engineering where you owned the *what* as well as the *how*. - **Curiosity that goes past the interface.** The strongest people here go and look at the data, the logs, the actual records, and the person doing the work, rather than asking someone to explain it. This is what we screen for hardest, and it's the thing we can't teach quickly. - **Writing other people act on:** a spec, a decision memo, an incident write-up. - **Comfort in front of an unhappy customer**, and the instinct to find out what's actually wrong before agreeing to anything. "I don't know yet, and here's when I will" is worth more than a fast answer. - **Enough SQL or spreadsheet fluency** to answer your own questions instead of waiting on someone else.

207388534e591639.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Metronome is a usage-based billing platform and a Stripe product. It helps modern software companies launch products faster, offer flexible pricing models, and streamline finance workflows.

The Metronome Integration Engineering team sits at the intersection of sales, growth, product, and research and development. We own the technical aspects of the customer lifecycle after a sale and before the customer transitions to our post-implementation teams.

What you'll do

As an Integration Engineer, you’ll help customers implement Metronome successfully and realize value quickly. You’ll lead technical work across requirements gathering, solution and integration design, configuration, testing, data migration, launch, and handoff.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct discovery and scoping to understand customers’ challenges across billing, product launches, pricing and packaging, quote-to-cash, customer experience, and related areas.
  • Support customers throughout the implementation lifecycle, including requirements gathering, technical design, integration design, testing, data migration, and launch.
  • Provide expert guidance on usage-based pricing and consumption-based business models.
  • Configure Metronome’s platform on behalf of customers.
  • Design integrations between Metronome’s APIs and customers’ business systems—including CRM and CPQ platforms, payment and tax systems, ERP and billing providers, and reporting and analytics tools—in alignment with Metronome best practices.
  • Serve as a liaison between customers and Metronome’s research and development teams, advocating for customer needs and feature requests.
  • Partner with implementation managers and other project-team members to provide visibility into progress and proactively identify risks and issues.
  • Build relationships across customer organizations, from day-to-day operators to C-suite executives. Meet customers in person when doing so will improve the engagement.
  • Advise customers on integrating Metronome into their systems and help shape their pricing and packaging strategies.
  • Ensure an effective handoff to Customer Success and Technical Support.

You’ll work with some of Metronome’s most strategic customers. These engagements will be complex, deep, and highly technical. Metronome directly influences how modern software companies monetize their products, and this team is on the front lines of that work.

Metronome operates with a startup mindset within Stripe. There is a significant opportunity for people with initiative to influence our direction, build processes from zero to one, and make a meaningful impact.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements below. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are helpful but not required.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in technical or customer-facing roles involving SaaS products, such as sales engineering, solutions architecture, technical account management, or deployment strategy.
  • Experience leading complex implementations for enterprise technology companies.
  • Experience working in fast-moving environments that value initiative and ownership.
  • Ability to quickly learn and communicate technical concepts to technical, go-to-market, and finance stakeholders.
  • Interest in building and improving go-to-market playbooks, processes, and reusable assets.
  • Ability to travel approximately 30% of the time, depending on customer needs.

Preferred qualifications

  • Deep knowledge of quote-to-cash processes, including experience integrating with or working alongside platforms such as Salesforce, NetSuite, CPQ systems, and the Stripe ecosystem.
  • Experience as a software engineer, product manager, or in another technical role.
  • Strong understanding of project- and program-management fundamentals.
  • Experience working with stakeholders in finance, engineering, product, sales operations, or billing operations.
  • Experience with logs, metrics, billing, finance, infrastructure, or financial tooling and concepts.

Job Title: AI Engineer Location: Pune, India (On-site), Type: Full-Time

Our client is building Last Mile 2.0 , redefining urban logistics in India. With proven MVP and are now scaling from pilot to national roll-out, looking for a AI Engineer to design, build, and scale the systems that will power thousands of riders across India.

Role Overview Were looking for AI Engineers and Researchers who can take ownership of building and deploying forecasting models into production. This isnt a research-only role its about getting working systems live, iterating fast, and making a measurable impact on SLA compliance.

Key Responsibilities:

Build and train forecasting models
Integrate model outputs into our real-time decision engine (Python APIs, Redis, AWS).
Work with simulation data to create training/evaluation sets.
Optimize for inference speed (ONNX/TorchScript, quantization).
Collaborate with the founders to shape model roadmap and metrics.

What Were Looking For:

Strong proficiency in Python + PyTorch/TensorFlow.
Experience with time-series models and data (any of: traffic, mobility, maps, forecasting).
Understanding of geospatial frameworks.
Comfort with data engineering basics (pipelines, ETL, SQL/NoSQL).
Ability to ship fast, debug, and optimize models for real-time serving.

Nice to have: Experience with Redis, OSRM, or similar real-time infra.

Background in last-mile logistics, ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery, or mobility data.
Exposure to reinforcement learning or simulation-driven training.

Why join us 

Early engineer role with high ownership.
Competitive salary + meaningful equity.
Opportunity to work on a hard real-world problem where ML decisions directly affect efficiency. .

201f5fbf901b933d.description: What role will you play in the team: As a Junior Product Analyst, you will support the product management team in understanding user behavior, identifying opportunities for product improvement, and contributing to data-driven decision-making. You will be responsible for collecting, analyzing, and reporting on key product metrics. What you will do: You will work closely with product managers, engineers, and designers to analyze product data, identify trends, and provide actionable insights. You will assist in conducting user research, A/B testing, and competitive analysis to inform product strategy and roadmap. Key responsibilities: Collect and analyze product data from various sources, including Google Analytics, Mixpanel, and customer feedback tools. Develop and maintain dashboards and reports to track key product metrics and performance. Conduct user research and A/B testing to gather insights and validate product hypotheses. Assist in identifying opportunities for product improvement and optimization. Collaborate with product managers and engineers to define and prioritize product requirements. Monitor and analyze competitor products and market trends. Present findings and recommendations to the product team and stakeholders. Support the product management team in developing and executing product roadmaps. Ensure data accuracy and integrity across all reporting and analysis. Stay up-to-date with the latest trends and best practices in product analytics. Required Qualification and Skills: Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as Computer Science, Statistics, or Business Administration. 0-1 year of experience in product analytics or a related field. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Proficiency in data analysis tools such as Google Analytics and Mixpanel. Experience with data visualization tools such as Tableau or Power BI (preferred). Familiarity with SQL and other database languages. Excellent communication and presentation skills. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. Understanding of Agile methodologies and product development lifecycle. Basic knowledge of statistical analysis and A/B testing principles. Benefits Included: Competitive salary and benefits package, including health insurance, paid time off, and retirement plan. Opportunities for professional development and growth within the company. Collaborative and supportive work environment. Exposure to cutting-edge technologies and product development practices. Flexible work arrangements, including remote work options. Employee assistance program (EAP) for personal and professional support. Regular team-building activities and social events. Performance-based bonuses and incentives. Employee discounts on company products and services. Comprehensive training and onboarding program. A Day in the Life: A typical day involves analyzing product data, creating reports, conducting user research, and collaborating with the product team to identify opportunities for improvement. You will also participate in team meetings and present your findings to stakeholders. .
